She doesn't see me approaching. My words grab her attention. I know why I'm here, let's just get this over with. You know, she says, obviously caught off guard. I knew a week ago. With watery eyes she says I can't see you anymore. We exchange the usual questions one would ask in this scenario.

Holding back tears, but only being partially successful, she says I'm trying not to make a scene. Correct me if I'm wrong, but a cramped coffee house, where I'm knocking elbows with strangers, isn't really the most appropriate venue for this sort of thing. But hey, it beats what I was rewarded with after our original three-year stint together, an out-of-nowhere phone call saying she's throwing her towel in. It's ok.

In the opening minute we have said all that needs to be said, yet I can tell we both have an urge to sit and savor our final moments together. Seasonal songs play over the speakers. Thanks Andy Williams, but it really isn't the most wonderful time of the year.
